```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6,
  fig.height = 4)
```

akeR calculates distances between microbiome samples and returns them as a
tidy data.frame, with the samples' metadata attached, ready to plot and
analyse. Everything goes through one function, `akeR()`, with two modes:

* **`mode = "reference"`**: the distance from each sample to a reference
  sample, such as its FMT donor or the subject's own baseline. The metadata
  needs a column (by default called `reference`) holding, for each sample,
  the ID of its reference sample. See `vignette("fmt", package = "akeR")`.
* **`mode = "group"`**: the distance between every pair of samples,
  labelled as within or between groups. Name the grouping column with
  `column`.

```{r setup}
library(akeR)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
```

## Input data

`akeR()` accepts:

* a matrix or data.frame of counts, taxa in rows and samples in columns
  (use `taxa_are_rows = FALSE` for the transpose), plus a metadata
  data.frame whose rownames are the sample names;
* a `phyloseq` object (metadata taken from `sample_data()`);
* a `SummarizedExperiment` / `TreeSummarizedExperiment`, such as the objects
  returned by curatedMetagenomicData (metadata taken from `colData()`);
* a precomputed `dist` object, plus metadata.

This vignette uses `family_example`, a **simulated** dataset of 12 families,
each with one mother and one infant sample. Infants carry some of their own
mother's taxa, and mothers and infants differ strongly as groups (see
`?family_example`).

```{r}
data(family_example)
counts <- family_example$counts
md <- family_example$metadata
head(md)
```

## Choosing a distance metric

`akeR_methods()` lists the metrics; pass one to `akeR()` with `method`.

```{r}
akeR_methods()[, c("method", "type", "description")]
```

* **Aitchison** (`"aitchison"`, the default) treats the data as
  compositional (CLR transform, then Euclidean distance) and suits shotgun
  metagenomic counts. Zeros need a pseudocount, and because of the log scale
  rare taxa carry real weight.
* **Robust Aitchison** (`"robust.aitchison"`) avoids pseudocounts by using
  only the non-zero taxa in each sample.
* **Bray-Curtis** (`"bray"`) is dominated by the most abundant taxa. akeR
  computes it on relative abundances, so sequencing depth does not drive it.
* **Jaccard / Sorensen** (`"jaccard"`, `"sorensen"`) use presence/absence
  only, so they measure which taxa are *shared*. That is often what matters
  for transmission or engraftment, but they depend on sequencing depth, so
  consider rarefying first.
* **Hellinger** and **Jensen-Shannon** (`"hellinger"`, `"jsd"`) sit in
  between.
* **UniFrac** (`"unifrac"`, `"wunifrac"`) needs a phyloseq object with a
  tree.

`calc_dist()` gives the distance matrix itself if you want it.

## Within and between groups

Do infants' microbiomes resemble their own mother's more than other
mothers'?

```{r}
fam <- akeR(counts, md, mode = "group", column = "family",
  method = "jaccard")
head(fam)
```

There is one row per pair of samples. `comparison` says whether the two
samples are from the same family, and every metadata column appears twice,
once for each sample (`role_1`, `role_2`, ...). That makes it easy to keep
only the pairs you want, here mother-infant pairs:

```{r}
mother_infant <- fam[fam$role_1 != fam$role_2, ]
aggregate(distance ~ comparison, data = mother_infant, FUN = median)
```

```{r}
ggboxplot(mother_infant, x = "comparison", y = "distance",
  fill = "comparison", add = "jitter", palette = "jco", legend = "none",
  xlab = "Mother-infant pairs", ylab = "Jaccard distance")
```

Mothers and their own infants share more taxa than unrelated mother-infant
pairs, as simulated.

### Comparing groups of pairs

Grouping by `role` instead gives three kinds of pairs: mother-mother,
infant-infant and mother-infant. `group_pair` labels them:

```{r}
roles <- akeR(counts, md, mode = "group", column = "role")
table(roles$group_pair)

ggplot(roles, aes(group_pair, distance, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.6, alpha = 0.4) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Aitchison distance", fill = NULL)
```

## Comparing metrics

Different metrics capture different things, so it is worth plotting the
same comparison with several:

```{r, fig.width = 7}
metrics <- c("aitchison", "robust.aitchison", "bray", "jaccard", "jsd")
by_metric <- do.call(rbind, lapply(metrics, function(m) {
  res <- akeR(counts, md, mode = "group", column = "family", method = m)
  res <- res[res$role_1 != res$role_2, ]
  data.frame(method = m, comparison = res$comparison,
    distance = res$distance)
}))

ggplot(by_metric, aes(comparison, distance, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~method, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Distance")
```

In the simulation, infants acquire their mother's taxa at fairly low
abundance. Presence/absence (Jaccard) and log-scale (Aitchison) metrics show
this clearly; Bray-Curtis and Jensen-Shannon, which are dominated by the
most abundant taxa, barely do.

## A note on statistical testing

akeR does not test the distances, because the right test depends on the
study design. One general caution: pairwise distances are not independent.
Each sample appears in many pairs, so a Wilcoxon or t-test on the rows of
the akeR output, which is what `ggpubr::stat_compare_means()` does, treats
correlated values as independent and gives p-values that are far too small.
Better options include permutation tests that shuffle labels across
*samples* (not pairs), PERMANOVA (`vegan::adonis2()`), or mixed models with
random effects for the samples or subjects involved.

## Real data from curatedMetagenomicData

`akeR()` takes a `TreeSummarizedExperiment` from curatedMetagenomicData
directly, using its `colData()` as metadata. Here is the same analysis on
real mother-infant data (Asnicar et al. 2017, *mSystems*). It needs an
internet connection, so it is not run here:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(curatedMetagenomicData)

tse <- curatedMetagenomicData("AsnicarF_2017.relative_abundance",
  counts = TRUE, dryrun = FALSE)[[1]]
tse <- tse[, tse$body_site == "stool"]
tse$family <- sub("^MV_FE[IM](\\d+)_.*$", "\\1", colnames(tse))
tse$role <- ifelse(grepl("^MV_FEM", colnames(tse)), "mother", "infant")

fam <- akeR(tse, mode = "group", column = "family", method = "jaccard")
fam <- fam[fam$role_1 != fam$role_2, ]
ggboxplot(fam, x = "comparison", y = "distance", add = "jitter")
```
